translation: There is pulse in the upper parts and no pulse in the lower parts; the person should vomit; [if] he does not vomit, [he] dies. What does it mean? 'No pulse in the lower parts' — this is what is called wood depression [mu yu]. [When] food and drink are overly satiated and stuff and fill the chest; the chest is the allotted domain of taiyin. The Classic states: "The qikou [pulse] on the contrary is larger than renying by three-fold; food injures taiyin." Hence it says: "If wood is depressed, reach it" — vomiting is this.
